question: How is the malaria parasite (Plasmodium) most commonly spread in Nigeria?

options.B: Bite of the female Anopheles mosquito

explanation: You've got this! Infected female Anopheles mosquitoes carry the malaria parasite and pass it into the bloodstream when they bite.

question: Which protozoal infection is mainly spread through contaminated food and water, often causing dysentery?
explanation: Great job! Ingesting Entamoeba histolytica cysts through dirty water or food can lead to painful amebic dysentery.

question: How do drugs like metronidazole mainly kill protozoa?

options.A: By disrupting DNA synthesis inside the parasite cell
options.B: By stimulating the human immune system to attack
options.C: By dissolving the outer cell wall using strong acids
options.D: By blocking the absorption of dietary calcium

explanation: Spot on! Metronidazole enters the parasite and creates reactive compounds that damage its DNA, stopping it from multiplying.

question: What is the main way classic quinoline antimalarial drugs work?

options.A: Binding directly to human liver cell receptors
options.B: Destroying the nervous system of the mosquito vector
options.C: Preventing the detoxification of heme inside the parasite
options.D: Enhancing the production of red blood cells in bone marrow

explanation: Well done! As the parasite digests red blood cells, it releases toxic heme. Quinoline drugs stop the parasite from turning this heme into safe crystals, effectively poisoning it.

question: Why is a luminal amebicide often given after a tissue amebicide like metronidazole?

options.A: To accelerate the renal excretion of the first drug
options.B: To permanently numb the lining of the stomach
options.C: To destroy cysts remaining in the gut lumen and prevent relapse
options.D: To quickly replenish lost electrolytes in the bloodstream

explanation: You're doing great! While metronidazole clears the tissue, luminal agents are needed to wipe out any sneaky cysts hiding in the gut so the infection doesn't return.

question: A patient finishes metronidazole for amebic dysentery but skips the luminal agent. What is the biggest risk?

options.A: Immediate development of permanent kidney failure
options.B: Severe permanent discoloration of the skin
options.C: Total immunity to all future bacterial infections
options.D: Relapse of the infection from surviving cysts in the gut

explanation: Exactly! Leftover cysts in the gut can hatch later and bring the infection right back, even if the patient felt better temporarily.

question: What is the main advantage of Artemisinin-based Combination Therapy (ACT)?

options.A: Making the medication taste significantly sweeter for children
options.B: Eliminating the need for any laboratory blood tests
options.C: Preventing drug resistance and clearing remaining parasites
options.D: Allowing the entire treatment course to last only one hour

explanation: Spot on! Combining a fast-acting drug with a partner drug clears the malaria completely and stops resistant strains from developing.

question: When is injectable artesunate preferred over oral malaria medications?

options.A: As a daily dietary supplement for pregnant women
options.B: When treating mild stomach ulcers caused by amoebas
options.C: In cases of severe, complicated malaria where oral intake is impossible
options.D: For routine outpatient prevention in healthy travelers

explanation: You got it! Severe malaria requires fast action through the IV or IM route because waiting on oral meds isn't safe for a very sick patient.

question: Why should patients take artemether-lumefantrine tablets with fatty food?

options.A: Fat neutralizes the bitter taste of the crushed tablets
options.B: Fat coats the stomach to completely prevent any nausea
options.C: Fat helps the kidneys excrete the drug much faster
options.D: Fat significantly improves the absorption of the lumefantrine component

explanation: Wonderful! Lumefantrine dissolves best in fat, so a fatty meal helps the body absorb it properly to knock out the malaria.

question: A patient taking oral metronidazole complains of stomach upset. What is the best nursing advice?

options.A: Crush the tablets and mix them into a citrus fruit juice
options.B: Double the next dose to compensate for the upset stomach
options.C: Take the medication with food or milk to ease gastric irritation
options.D: Stop taking the medication immediately and discard the remaining pills

explanation: Correct! Metronidazole can be tough on the tummy, but taking it with meals or milk helps soothe the stomach without losing drug power.

question: What bad reaction happens if someone drinks alcohol while taking metronidazole?

options.A: Immediate and permanent loss of hearing in both ears
options.B: A sudden spike in blood pressure leading to stroke
options.C: A disulfiram-like reaction with flushing, vomiting, and severe headache
options.D: Total paralysis of the lower skeletal muscles

explanation: Spot on! Mixing metronidazole and alcohol causes a nasty reaction (flushing, vomiting, pounding headache) because the drug blocks alcohol breakdown.

question: Which symptom is a classic sign of cinchonism in a patient taking quinine?
explanation: You're doing great! Tinnitus (ringing in the ears), dizziness, and mild blurred vision are hallmark clues of quinine overdose (cinchonism).

question: Why is checking pregnancy status crucial before giving certain antiprotozoal drugs?

options.A: Pregnant women do not absorb any active ingredients from oral tablets
options.B: Pregnancy completely destroys the ability of the liver to metabolize drugs
options.C: Antimalarial drugs cause instant miscarriage in all trimesters
options.D: Many antiprotozoal agents are teratogenic and contraindicated in early pregnancy

explanation: Brilliant! Some antiprotozoal drugs can harm fetal development, making a pregnancy check an essential safety step.

question: A patient on IV quinine for severe malaria reports dizziness and ringing in the ears. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Assume this is a normal side effect and document it routinely
options.B: Notify the prescriber and evaluate for signs of quinine toxicity
options.C: Stop the intravenous line permanently without telling anyone
options.D: Encourage the patient to drink large volumes of cold water

explanation: Spot on! These are classic signs of cinchonism (quinine toxicity). The doctor must be informed right away to keep the patient safe.

question: What is one of the best ways patients can prevent malaria at home?

options.A: Avoiding all contact with domestic farm animals
options.B: Boiling all household cooking oil before use
options.C: Taking a daily dose of metronidazole as a vitamin
options.D: Sleeping under insecticide-treated bed nets every night

explanation: You've got this! Insecticide-treated nets create a protective shield against those nighttime Anopheles mosquito bites.

question: Why must patients finish all their antiprotozoal medication even after feeling better?

options.A: Incomplete courses cause permanent damage to human taste buds
options.B: Leftover pills lose their chemical stability and become poisonous
options.C: Health clinics charge heavy fines for unfinished medicine bottles
options.D: Stopping early can leave surviving parasites and cause a relapse

explanation: Amazing work! Feeling better doesn't mean all parasites are gone. Finishing the dose ensures the infection won't bounce back.
